title: Recipe Book
blurb: Sixteen high-protein recipes, each scaled to three portions: two for tonight and one to spare.

recipes.time: Prep 15 min + 20 min marinate · Cook 35 min
recipes.eq: Large deep skillet or Dutch oven, pot or rice cooker
i: 675 g chicken breast, cut into 1-inch cubes
½ cup + 1 tbsp 0% plain Greek yogurt
¾ tsp salt, divided, plus more to taste
¾ tsp chili powder (optional, for heat)
¾ cup dry basmati rice, plus 1 cup + 2 tbsp water
Small handful cilantro, chopped, to finish
s: Marinate|In a bowl, mix ½ cup + 1 tbsp Greek yogurt, 2 tsp garam masala and ½ tsp salt. Add the 675 g chicken cubes and stir until every piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate at least 20 minutes (up to overnight for more flavour).

Start the rice|Rinse ¾ cup basmati in a sieve under cold water until the water runs mostly clear (about 30 seconds). Add the rice and 1 cup + 2 tbsp water to a pot with a pinch of salt, bring to a boil, then cover, drop to the lowest heat and cook 12 minutes. Turn off the heat and leave it covered 10 minutes, then fluff with a fork. (Or use a rice cooker.)

Sear the chicken|Heat 2 tsp oil in your large skillet over medium-high until it shimmers. Shake excess marinade off the chicken and add it in a single layer (do this in 2 batches if it doesn't fit). Leave it untouched 3 minutes so it browns, then flip and cook 2 more minutes. It doesn't need to be cooked through yet. Move to a plate.

Build the sauce base|Lower heat to medium. Add 1½ tbsp butter to the same pan (don't clean it; the browned bits are flavour). Once melted, add the diced onion and a pinch of salt and cook, stirring occasionally, 6–8 minutes until soft and light golden.
Bloom the spices|Add 2 tsp garlic, 2 tsp ginger, the remaining 2 tsp garam masala and ¾ tsp chili powder. Stir constantly for 60 seconds until very fragrant. Don't let the garlic brown.
Simmer|Pour in 1 cup + 2 tbsp passata and the remaining ¼ tsp salt, stir, and bring to a gentle bubble. Cook 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until it thickens slightly and darkens in colour.

Finish|Stir in 6 tbsp coconut milk, then return the chicken and any juices from the plate. Simmer uncovered 8–10 minutes until the chicken is cooked through (no pink in the centre, 165°F/74°C). Taste and add salt if needed. If the sauce gets too thick, splash in water.

Serve|Split the rice three ways (about ¾ cup cooked each), spoon chicken and sauce alongside, and top with cilantro. Two portions for tonight. Let the third cool 20 minutes before it goes in the fridge.
recipes.rh: Microwave covered 2–2½ minutes, stirring halfway. Add a splash of water to the rice.
recipes.x: The spare keeps 4 days in the fridge.

recipes.eq: Large skillet, pot or rice cooker
i: 2 tsp chipotle in adobo, finely chopped (plus ¾ tsp of the sauce)
1 can (398 ml) black beans, drained and rinsed
¾ cup dry rice, plus 1½ cups water (1 cup + 2 tbsp for basmati)
s: Start the rice|Rinse ¾ cup rice, then add it to a pot with 1½ cups water (1 cup + 2 tbsp for basmati) and a pinch of salt. Boil, cover, reduce to low and cook 15 minutes (12 for basmati). Rest covered 10 minutes off the heat.

Brown the turkey|Heat 2 tsp oil in your large skillet over medium-high. Add 675 g turkey and break it apart with a wooden spoon. Cook 7–9 minutes, stirring every minute or so, until no pink remains and some bits are browned. Turkey is lean, so don't expect much fat; if a little collects, leave it.

Season|Sprinkle in 2 tsp chili powder, 1½ tsp cumin, ¾ tsp smoked paprika, ¾ tsp garlic powder and ¾ tsp salt. Add 2 tsp chopped chipotle and ¾ tsp adobo sauce. Stir 1 minute to toast the spices, then pour in 6 tbsp water and scrape the bottom of the pan. Simmer 3 minutes until the liquid mostly cooks off and coats the meat.

Add beans and corn|Stir in the drained black beans and ¾ cup frozen corn. Cook 3–4 minutes until everything is hot. Squeeze in the juice of half a lime. Taste; add more salt or chipotle if you want more kick.
Make lime rice|Fluff the rice, then stir in the zest and juice of 1 lime and the cilantro.

Serve|Split the rice three ways and top with the turkey mixture. Add ¼ cup salsa, 2 tbsp yogurt and a handful of shredded romaine to each of tonight's two bowls. Box the third without the cold toppings and add them after reheating.
recipes.rh: Microwave rice and turkey 2 minutes. Top with cold salsa, yogurt and romaine after heating.
recipes.x: Swap in extra-lean ground beef any week; drain any fat after browning.

recipes.eq: Sheet pan, cast iron or heavy skillet, sturdy flat spatula
i: Scant ½ tsp garlic powder, plus salt and pepper, for the potatoes
¾ tsp salt and a scant ½ tsp pepper, for the beef
Pinch each of paprika and garlic powder
s: Roast the potatoes|Heat oven to 425°F (220°C). On a sheet pan, toss 600 g potato halves with 2 tsp olive oil, a scant ½ tsp garlic powder and a good pinch of salt and pepper. Turn them cut side down. Roast 25–30 minutes until the undersides are deep golden and a fork slides in easily. No need to flip.

Make the sauce|While the potatoes roast, stir 6 tbsp Greek yogurt, 1½ tbsp light mayo, 2 tsp ketchup, ¾ tsp yellow mustard, 1½ tbsp relish and a pinch each of paprika and garlic powder in a small bowl. Taste; add more relish for tang or ketchup for sweetness. Refrigerate.
Portion the beef|Divide 675 g beef into 6 loose balls (about 110 g each). Don't pack them tight; loose meat smashes thinner and browns better.
Heat the pan hard|Put your cast iron over high heat for 3–4 minutes with no oil, until it's smoking lightly. Open a window or turn on the fan.

Smash|Place 2–3 balls in the pan with space between. Immediately press each one flat with your spatula as hard as you can (a piece of parchment between the spatula and meat stops sticking) to about ¼ inch thick. Season the tops, using ¾ tsp salt and a scant ½ tsp pepper across all six.

Flip and melt|Cook 2 minutes without moving until the edges are dark brown and crisp. Scrape under each patty firmly with the spatula to keep the crust, flip, and lay half a cheese slice on each. Cook 1 more minute. Repeat with the rest, wiping out the pan between batches if it gets too smoky.

Chop and serve|Let the patties rest 2 minutes, then roughly chop them. Split the potatoes and beef three ways. Top tonight's two bowls with romaine, tomato, red onion, pickles and sauce. Box the third with its salad and sauce kept separate.
recipes.rh: Microwave potatoes and beef 1½–2 minutes (or air fry 4 minutes at 375°F to re-crisp). Add cold salad and sauce after.

recipes.t: Sticky, sweet, the one you'll repeat.
recipes.eq: Sheet pan, large skillet, pot or rice cooker
i: 675 g chicken breast, cut into 1-inch cubes
Scant ½ tsp salt and a pinch of pepper
450 g broccoli florets + ¾ tsp oil
¾ cup dry rice, plus 1½ cups water
Sesame seeds and sliced green onion, to finish
s: Prep|Heat oven to 425°F (220°C). Start the rice: rinse ¾ cup, boil in 1½ cups water, cover on low 15 minutes, rest 10. In a small bowl, whisk 2 tbsp honey, 3 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tsp garlic and 2 tsp rice vinegar; set aside. In a cup, stir 2 tsp cornstarch into 1½ tbsp cold water for the slurry.
Roast the broccoli|Toss 450 g florets with ¾ tsp oil and a pinch of salt on a sheet pan. Roast 15–18 minutes until the edges are browned and crispy.
Coat the chicken|Pat 675 g chicken dry with paper towel. Toss with a scant ½ tsp salt, a pinch of pepper and 2 tsp cornstarch. This thin coating is what makes the sauce cling and turn sticky.

Sear|Heat 2 tsp oil in your large skillet over medium-high until shimmering. Add chicken in a single layer (2 batches if needed). Cook 3 minutes without touching, flip, and cook 3–4 more until golden and cooked through (165°F/74°C, no pink inside).
Sauce|Return all chicken to the pan and drop heat to medium. Pour in the honey-soy mixture; it will bubble fast. Stir 1–2 minutes.
Thicken|Stir the slurry again (it settles), pour it in and stir constantly 30–60 seconds until the sauce turns glossy and coats the chicken. Take it off the heat immediately; honey burns quickly.
Serve|Split the rice, broccoli and chicken three ways and spoon all the pan sauce over. Scatter sesame seeds and green onion. Two portions for tonight, the third into a container once it has cooled.
recipes.rh: Microwave covered 2 minutes. The sauce loosens as it warms.

recipes.eq: Sheet pan, large skillet, small saucepan, pot or rice cooker
i: 600 g chicken breast, cut into 1-inch cubes
¾ tsp garlic powder, ¾ tsp paprika, scant ½ tsp salt and a pinch of pepper
525 g broccoli florets + ¾ tsp oil
¾ cup dry rice, plus 1½ cups water
280 ml 2% evaporated milk (¾ of a 370 ml can)
Pinch each of garlic powder and cayenne
s: Start the rice and oven|Heat oven to 425°F (220°C). Rinse ¾ cup rice and cook in 1½ cups water (boil, cover, lowest heat 15 minutes, rest 10).
Roast the broccoli|Toss 525 g florets with ¾ tsp oil and a pinch of salt on a sheet pan. Roast 15–18 minutes until tender with crispy browned edges.

Cook the chicken|Toss 600 g chicken with ¾ tsp garlic powder, ¾ tsp paprika, a scant ½ tsp salt and a pinch of pepper. Heat 2 tsp oil in your skillet over medium-high until shimmering. Add chicken in one layer (2 batches if needed), cook 3 minutes untouched, flip, and cook 3–4 more minutes until golden and 165°F/74°C inside.

Heat the milk|For the sauce, pour all but 2 tbsp of the 280 ml evaporated milk into a small saucepan over medium heat. Heat until steaming with small bubbles at the edge, about 3 minutes. Don't let it boil hard.
Thicken|Stir 2 tsp cornstarch into the reserved 2 tbsp cold evaporated milk until smooth. Whisk it into the hot milk and keep whisking 1–2 minutes until it thickens enough to coat a spoon.

Melt in the cheese|Take the pan off the heat. Add 90 g cheddar a handful at a time, whisking until each addition melts before adding more. Stir in a scant ½ tsp Dijon, a pinch each of garlic powder and cayenne, and salt to taste. Off-heat melting keeps it smooth instead of grainy.
Serve|Split the rice, broccoli and chicken three ways and pour the cheese sauce over the broccoli and chicken. For the spare, pack its sauce in a small cup if you like it saucier after reheating.
recipes.rh: Microwave covered 2 minutes, stirring halfway. If the sauce has set, stir in 1 tbsp milk.
recipes.x: Evaporated milk is the trick: it gives a cream-sauce texture for a fraction of the fat. Sauce keeps 4 days.

i: ¾ tsp Italian seasoning, scant ½ tsp salt and a pinch of pepper
255 g chickpea or lentil pasta, penne or rotini (¾ of a 340 g box)
s: Even out the chicken|If the breasts are thick on one end, place them between plastic wrap and pound with a pan or rolling pin to an even ¾ inch. They'll cook evenly and stay juicy. Season both sides with ¾ tsp Italian seasoning, a scant ½ tsp salt and a pinch of pepper.

Cook the chicken|Heat 2 tsp olive oil in your skillet over medium-high. Lay the 600 g chicken in and don't move it for 5–6 minutes until deep golden. Flip, turn heat to medium, and cook 5–6 more minutes until the thickest part reads 165°F/74°C or the juices run clear when cut. Rest on a board 5 minutes, then slice.

Boil the pasta|Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a rolling boil. Cook 255 g pasta 1 minute less than the package says; legume pasta goes mushy fast. Before draining, scoop out ½ cup of the pasta water.
Wilt the veg|Drain the pasta and return it to the hot pot off the heat. Add 2 handfuls spinach and 1½ cups halved tomatoes and stir; the heat will wilt the spinach in about a minute.
Sauce it|Add ¼ cup pesto and 2–3 tbsp of the reserved pasta water. Stir well until the pesto coats everything in a loose sauce (add more water if it looks dry).
Finish and serve|Fold in the sliced chicken and ¼ cup parmesan. Split three ways: two for tonight, one for the fridge.
recipes.rh: Add 1 tbsp water, microwave covered 1½–2 minutes, stir. Also good cold like pasta salad.
recipes.x: The spare keeps 3 days and is also good cold.

recipes.time: Prep 20 min + 20 min marinate · Cook 25 min
recipes.eq: Sheet pan or skillet, box grater, pot
i: 2 tbsp lemon juice (from 1 lemon; keep the rest)
¾ tsp minced garlic (1 small clove)
2 tsp fresh dill (or ¾ tsp dried)
Squeeze of lemon and a pinch of salt
¾ cup dry rice or orzo (rice needs 1½ cups water)
s: Marinate|Whisk 2 tbsp lemon juice, 2 tsp olive oil, 2 tsp garlic, 1½ tsp oregano, ¾ tsp paprika, ¾ tsp salt and a scant ½ tsp pepper in a bowl or zip bag. Add 675 g chicken thighs and massage to coat. Refrigerate at least 20 minutes (up to 24 hours).

Start the rice or orzo|Rice: rinse ¾ cup and cook in 1½ cups water, 15 minutes on low, rest 10. Orzo: boil ¾ cup in salted water 8–9 minutes, drain, and toss with a few drops of olive oil so it doesn't clump.

Cook the chicken|Heat oven to 425°F (220°C). Lay thighs flat on a lined sheet pan with space between them. Roast 18–22 minutes until the edges char slightly and the thickest piece reads 175°F/80°C (thighs taste better cooked a bit past 165°F). For more colour, broil the last 2 minutes. Or pan-fry over medium-high, 5–6 minutes per side.

Make the tzatziki|Grate ⅓ of a cucumber on the large holes of a box grater. Pile it in a clean towel and squeeze hard over the sink until no more water comes out; this stops the sauce going runny. Mix with ¾ cup yogurt, ¾ tsp garlic, 2 tsp dill, ¾ tsp lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Make the salad|Toss the diced ⅔ cucumber, 2 small tomatoes and ⅓ red onion with a squeeze of lemon and a pinch of salt. Keep it separate from hot food.
Slice|Rest the chicken 5 minutes, then slice into strips.
Serve|Split the rice, chicken and ¼ cup feta three ways. Add salad and tzatziki to tonight's two bowls. Pack the spare's salad and tzatziki separately so the rice doesn't get soggy.
recipes.rh: Microwave rice and chicken 2 minutes. Add cold salad and tzatziki after.

recipes.eq: Lined sheet pan, small saucepan, pot
i: 3 salmon fillets, about 150 g each, skin on or off
¾ tsp minced garlic (1 small clove)
¾ cup dry rice, plus 1½ cups water
Sesame seeds and sliced green onion, to finish
s: Make the teriyaki|In a small saucepan, whisk 3 tbsp soy sauce, 1½ tbsp honey, 2 tsp rice vinegar, ¾ tsp garlic, ¾ tsp ginger, 1½ tbsp water and ¾ tsp cornstarch. Bring to a simmer over medium, stirring, and cook 1–2 minutes until it thickens enough to coat a spoon. Pour half into a separate bowl for brushing (so the raw-fish brush never touches the serving sauce).
Start the rice|Rinse ¾ cup rice and cook in 1½ cups water (boil, cover on low 15 minutes, rest 10).
Prep the salmon|Heat oven to 400°F (200°C). Pat the 3 fillets dry, place on a lined sheet pan skin side down, and season lightly with salt. Brush generously with the brushing half of the sauce.

Bake|Bake 12–14 minutes, until the salmon flakes easily at the thickest point and reads 130–140°F (54–60°C). It will keep cooking a little on the tray. For a glazed top, brush once more and broil 1–2 minutes, watching closely.
Cook the edamame|Boil or microwave 1¼ cups edamame 3–4 minutes until hot, drain, and salt lightly.

Serve|Split the rice three ways. Add a fillet, edamame, sliced cucumber and carrot to each. Drizzle the reserved teriyaki over the salmon and finish with sesame seeds and green onion. Two for tonight, one for the fridge.
recipes.rh: Microwave at 50% power for 2–2½ minutes to avoid drying out the salmon, or eat it cold over warm rice.
recipes.x: The spare keeps 2 days in the fridge.

recipes.t: Egg-dipped cod, lemon butter and wine sauce.
recipes.eq: Sheet pan, large non-stick skillet, 3 shallow dishes
i: 675 g cod fillets, cut into 3 portions
Scant ½ tsp salt and a pinch of pepper
¾ tsp minced garlic (1 small clove)
6 tbsp dry white wine (or extra broth)
2 tbsp lemon juice (about ¾ of a lemon)
600 g baby potatoes, halved + ¾ tsp oil
s: Roast the potatoes|Heat oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss 600 g potatoes with ¾ tsp oil, salt and pepper, turn cut side down on a sheet pan, and roast 25–30 minutes. Add 300 g green beans to the same pan for the last 12 minutes.
Set up the station|Put ¼ cup flour in one shallow dish. Whisk 2 eggs, 1½ tbsp parmesan and 2 tsp parsley in a second. Leave a clean plate at the end.
Dry and season the fish|Pat the cod very dry with paper towel; wet fish makes the coating slide off. Season both sides with a scant ½ tsp salt and a pinch of pepper.
Dredge and dip|Coat each piece lightly in flour and tap off the excess, then dip in the egg mixture so it's fully covered, letting extra drip back into the dish.

Pan-fry|Heat 2 tsp butter and 2 tsp oil in the skillet over medium until the butter foams. Lay the cod in (don't crowd it) and cook 3–4 minutes until the underside is golden. Flip gently with a fish spatula and cook 3–4 more minutes until the thickest part flakes easily and is opaque all the way through (145°F/63°C). Move to a plate.

Build the sauce|Wipe out any burnt bits but leave the golden ones. Over medium, melt 2 tsp butter and add ¾ tsp garlic for 30 seconds. Pour in 6 tbsp wine and let it bubble 2 minutes until reduced by half. Add 6 tbsp broth and 2 tbsp lemon juice and simmer 3 minutes.
Finish the sauce|Take the pan off the heat and swirl in 2 tsp cold butter until the sauce turns slightly glossy. Stir in 2 tsp capers and a little parsley. Taste for salt.
Serve|Split the potatoes, green beans and cod three ways and pour the sauce over tonight's two plates. Pack the spare's sauce in a small cup so the coating stays intact; pour it over after reheating.
recipes.rh: Best: oven or air fryer at 350°F for 6–8 minutes. Otherwise microwave at 50% power for 1½–2 minutes. Warm the sauce separately and pour over.
recipes.x: The spare keeps 2 days. Sole or haddock work the same way.

recipes.t: Silky cream sauce, fruity peppery bite.
recipes.eq: Sheet pan, large skillet, pot or rice cooker, mortar or zip bag
i: 675 g haddock (or halibut or cod), cut into 3 portions
Scant ½ tsp salt and a pinch of black pepper
¾ cup dry jasmine rice, plus 1 cup + 2 tbsp water
1 small bunch asparagus, woody ends snapped off + ¾ tsp oil
¼ cup dry white wine (or broth)
s: Rice and asparagus|Cook the rice (rinse ¾ cup, add 1 cup + 2 tbsp water, boil, cover on low 15 minutes, rest 10). Heat oven to 425°F (220°C), toss the asparagus with ¾ tsp oil and a pinch of salt, and roast 10–12 minutes until just tender.
Crush the peppercorns|Put 2 tsp pink peppercorns in a zip bag and press with the bottom of a pan, or use a mortar. You want them cracked, not powdered.

Sear the fish|Pat the haddock very dry and season with a scant ½ tsp salt and a pinch of pepper. Heat 2 tsp oil in the skillet over medium-high until shimmering. Lay the fish in and cook 3 minutes without moving until golden underneath. Flip carefully and cook 2–3 minutes more until opaque and flaking at the thickest part. Move to a plate.
Start the sauce|Lower heat to medium. Add 2 tsp butter and the diced shallot and cook 2–3 minutes until soft. Add most of the pink peppercorns (save a pinch for garnish) and stir 30 seconds.
Reduce|Pour in ¼ cup wine and let it bubble 2 minutes until reduced by about half.

Make it creamy|Lower to medium-low. Stir in ½ cup evaporated milk and ¾ tsp Dijon and simmer gently 3–4 minutes until it thickens enough to coat a spoon. Keep it at a gentle bubble; a hard boil can split it. Add a squeeze of lemon, salt to taste and chives.
Serve|Split the rice, asparagus and fish three ways. Spoon sauce over the fish and finish with the reserved peppercorns. Two for tonight, one for the fridge.
recipes.rh: Microwave at 50% power for 2–2½ minutes to keep the fish tender.
recipes.x: The spare keeps 2 days. Pink peppercorns are related to cashews, so skip them if anyone eating has a cashew allergy.

recipes.time: Prep 15 min + 30 min soak · Cook 35 min
recipes.eq: Air fryer or sheet pan, cast iron skillet, meat thermometer
i: 675 g top sirloin, 2–3 steaks about 1 inch thick
¾ tsp salt and ¾ tsp coarse black pepper
2 tsp butter, 2 garlic cloves (smashed) and 2 sprigs thyme, for basting
2 tsp oil and a scant ½ tsp salt
2 handfuls arugula and a squeeze of lemon
s: Cut and soak the fries|Cut 600 g potatoes (skin on is fine) into ⅓-inch sticks. Soak in cold water 30 minutes. This pulls out surface starch so they crisp instead of going limp.
Temper the steak|While the fries soak, take the steak out of the fridge, pat it very dry, and season both sides with ¾ tsp salt and ¾ tsp pepper. Leave it on the counter.

Cook the fries|Drain the fries and dry them thoroughly with a towel (water is the enemy of crisp). Toss with 2 tsp oil and a scant ½ tsp salt. Air fryer: 380°F for 18–22 minutes, shaking every 6 minutes. Oven: spread in one layer on parchment at 450°F for 30–35 minutes, flipping halfway.

Make the béarnaise|Stir 6 tbsp yogurt, 2 tsp melted butter, ¾ tsp Dijon, ¾ tsp tarragon, the minced shallot, ¾ tsp lemon juice and a pinch of salt together. Let it sit 10 minutes so the tarragon softens.

Sear the steak|Heat cast iron over high until it just starts to smoke. Add ¾ tsp oil, then the steaks. Don't touch them for 3 minutes. Flip and cook 2–3 minutes more. Aim for 130°F (54°C) inside for medium-rare; it climbs a few degrees while it rests.
Baste|Turn heat to medium, add 2 tsp butter, 2 smashed garlic cloves and 2 thyme sprigs. Tilt the pan and spoon the foaming butter over the steaks for 45 seconds.
Rest and slice|Rest the steaks on a board 10 minutes, then slice across the grain into strips.
Serve|Split the steak and fries three ways. Add arugula with a squeeze of lemon and béarnaise to tonight's two plates. Pack the spare's arugula and béarnaise separately.
recipes.rh: Fries: air fry at 375°F for 4–5 minutes to re-crisp. Steak: microwave at 50% for 30–45 seconds, or eat it cold sliced. Add arugula and béarnaise after.
recipes.x: The spare keeps 3 days. Flank or striploin also work.

recipes.eq: Oven-safe skillet, pot, potato masher, meat thermometer
i: 750 g pork tenderloin (1 large or 2 small)
¾ tsp salt, scant ½ tsp pepper and ¾ tsp dried thyme
¾ tsp minced garlic (1 small clove)
s: Trim the pork|Heat oven to 400°F (200°C). Look for the thin shiny membrane (silverskin) on the tenderloin. Slide a knife just under it and cut it away, angling the blade up; it turns chewy if left on. Season all over with ¾ tsp salt, a scant ½ tsp pepper and ¾ tsp thyme.

Start the mash|Peel 600 g potatoes and cube into 1½-inch pieces. Put in a pot, cover with cold water, add ¾ tsp salt, and bring to a boil. Simmer 15 minutes until a fork slides through with no resistance.
Sear the pork|Heat 2 tsp oil in the oven-safe skillet over medium-high. Sear the pork on all sides, about 2 minutes per side, 6–8 minutes total, until browned.

Roast|Move the skillet to the oven and roast 12–15 minutes until the centre reads 145°F/63°C. A little pink inside is correct and safe. Move the pork to a board and rest 10 minutes. Leave a towel over the hot skillet handle.
Finish the mash|Drain the potatoes well and let them steam dry 1 minute in the pot. Mash with 2 tsp butter, then stir in ¼ cup yogurt and 3 tbsp milk until creamy. Season with salt and pepper.
Cook the green beans|Steam or microwave 300 g beans with 2 tbsp water, covered, 4 minutes until bright green and tender-crisp. Salt lightly.

Make the sauce|Put the skillet back on the stove over medium (the handle is still hot). Add ¾ tsp butter and the shallot for 2 minutes, then ¾ tsp garlic for 30 seconds. Pour in 6 tbsp broth and scrape up the browned bits; simmer 3 minutes until reduced by half. Stir in ½ cup evaporated milk, 2 tsp Dijon, 2 tsp grainy mustard and a scant ½ tsp thyme. Simmer gently 3–4 minutes until it coats a spoon. Add pepper and pour in any juices from the resting pork.
Slice and serve|Slice the pork into ½-inch medallions. Split the mash, beans and pork three ways and spoon sauce over the pork so it stays moist. Two for tonight, one for the fridge.
recipes.rh: Microwave covered 2 minutes, with the sauce over the pork. Add a splash of milk to the mash if it's stiff.

recipes.eq: Large bowl, whisk, 4 jars or containers
i: Pinch of salt and a scant ½ tsp cinnamon (optional)
s: Dissolve the protein first|Pour 1½ cups milk into a large bowl, add 3 scoops protein powder, and whisk hard for 30 seconds until completely smooth. Doing this first prevents dry clumps later.

Mix the base|Whisk in ¾ cup Greek yogurt, then stir in 1½ cups oats, 1½ tbsp chia, a pinch of salt and the cinnamon until evenly combined. It should look loose and soupy; the oats and chia absorb a lot of liquid overnight.
Jar it|Divide evenly between 3 jars. Top each with ½ cup frozen berries. Frozen is fine; they thaw overnight and bleed flavour into the oats.
Chill|Seal and refrigerate at least 6 hours or overnight.
Adjust in the morning|If it's too thick, stir in a splash of milk. Eat cold, or microwave 60–90 seconds if you prefer it warm.
recipes.x: Makes 3 jars, which keep 4 days. Swap in chocolate protein and add a tbsp of peanut butter for variety.

recipes.time: Prep 20 min · Cook 20 min · Cool 20 min
recipes.eq: Large non-stick skillet, foil, freezer bag
i: Scant ½ tsp salt and a pinch of pepper
s: Cook the filling|Brown 190 g sausage in the skillet over medium-high, breaking it into small crumbles, 6–7 minutes. Add the diced peppers and onion and cook 5 more minutes until soft and any liquid has cooked off. Wet filling makes soggy burritos, so get it dry. Tip into a bowl.

Scramble the eggs|Whisk 6 eggs, 375 ml egg whites, a scant ½ tsp salt and a pinch of pepper. Wipe the pan, spray it, and set to medium-low. Pour in the eggs and let sit 30 seconds, then slowly push them from the edges to the centre with a spatula. Stop while they still look slightly wet (about 4–5 minutes); they finish cooking when reheated.
Cool the fillings|Spread the eggs on a plate and let both fillings cool 10 minutes. Hot filling steams inside the wrap and causes ice crystals and sogginess.
Warm the tortillas|Microwave the stack of 6 tortillas under a damp paper towel for 30 seconds so they fold without cracking.

Assemble|Lay a tortilla flat. In the lower third, add a sixth of the eggs, a sixth of the sausage mix, 2 tbsp cheese and 1 tbsp salsa. Fold the bottom edge up over the filling, fold in both sides, then roll up tightly away from you.
Wrap and freeze|Eat two now if you like. Wrap the rest tightly in foil (or plastic wrap), label with the date, and put them in a large freezer bag. Freeze flat.
recipes.rh: From frozen: remove foil, wrap in a damp paper towel, microwave 1 minute, flip, 1–1½ more minutes until hot in the centre. For a crisp outside, finish 2 minutes in a dry pan or air fryer.
recipes.x: Makes 6 burritos; two are one portion. They keep 2 months frozen.

i: Salt, pepper and a pinch of garlic powder, for the chicken
¾ tsp lemon juice and plenty of cracked pepper
s: Cook the chicken|Season 450 g chicken breast with salt, pepper and a pinch of garlic powder. Pan-cook in 1 tsp oil over medium-high, 5–6 minutes per side, to 165°F/74°C. Rest 5 minutes and slice thinly.
Crisp the bacon|Cook 3 strips turkey bacon in a dry skillet over medium, 3–4 minutes per side, until crisp. Cool on paper towel, then crumble.
Mix the dressing|Stir 2 tbsp Caesar dressing, 2 tbsp Greek yogurt, ¾ tsp lemon juice and lots of pepper together. The yogurt adds protein and cuts calories without losing the flavour.
Dry the romaine|Make sure the chopped romaine is completely dry (use a salad spinner or towel). Wet lettuce makes wraps soggy.
Toss|In a large bowl, toss the romaine, chicken, bacon and 3 tbsp parmesan with the dressing until everything is lightly coated.

Roll|Warm 3 tortillas 20 seconds in the microwave. Pile a third of the filling in the lower third of each, fold up the bottom, fold in the sides, and roll tightly. Cut tonight's two in half. Wrap the spare in foil.
recipes.rh: Eat the spare cold, within 2 days.
recipes.x: For a crisper spare, set its share aside before dressing and toss it when you eat it.

recipes.t: Tastes like dessert, eats like a shake.
i: Berries or a few chocolate chips to top (optional)
s: Combine the dry|In a bowl, mix 1½ scoops protein powder, 2 tsp cocoa and a pinch of salt so the cocoa doesn't clump.
Whisk in the yogurt|Add 2¼ cups (560 g) yogurt and whisk hard for about a minute. It will look stiff and streaky at first, then turn smooth and dark.
Adjust the texture|Add 2–3 tbsp milk, 1 tbsp at a time, whisking between, until it's thick and spoonable like pudding. Different protein powders absorb different amounts, so go by feel.
Chill|Split between 3 bowls or containers and refrigerate at least 1 hour. It thickens as it sits. Top right before eating.

fine: Macros are estimates per portion, based on standard grocery products. Amounts on the list are what the recipes use, so check the pantry before buying spices and sauces.

snacks.note: A 50 g bag. Check sugar; teriyaki styles are the worst offenders.
Two sticks. Keeps in a bag or the car forever.
Sea salt or BBQ. Crunchy, the closest thing to chips with fibre.
A small handful, about 30 g. Buy the portion packs if the big bag disappears.
Quest or Legendary. Scratches the crisps itch for real protein.
A tub with everything-bagel seasoning and crackers. Cheap protein.
Two rounds. Fridge staple that survives a backpack.
